newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Dozen new Russian ADRs issues in works - bank.
newsitem.headline: Dozen new Russian ADRs issues in works - bank.

text.p: At least a dozen Russian firms are preparing new issues of ADRs, including one planning to list a level-three issue before the end of the year, a senior banker said on Thursday.

Christopher Sturdy, vice president of depositary receipts at the Bank of New York in London, told an investment conference the bank was in talks with clients on nine level-one ADR issues, two private placements and the prospective level three listing.
Sturdy said the timing of the level-three issue, which raises new capital and requires strict disclosure of a company's financial performance, would depend on market conditions.
"It could be before the end of the year," he said, but declined to name the company.

Several Russian companies, including high-profile firms such as LUKoil and Chernogorneft, have issued level one ADRs, which are intended to increase liquidity in a stocks but do not raise new capital.
The Bank of New York is depositary bank to many issues.
Mosenergo has made a private placement of treasury stock.
Russian banks also plan to issue ADRs, which allow foreign investors to gain access to underlying shares without domestic settlement problems, but need central bank approval first.
Sturdy said some 23 percent of Mosenergo shares were held in ADR form, 22 percent for LUKoil and 14 percent for Seversky Tube Works.
"I think that is a very positive sign of the interest across the globe in investing in Russian stocks," Sturdy said.
Companies which have announced plans for ADRs include Unified Energy System and Irkutskenerg.

"There is a relatively large number of companies which are either in a position to appeal to international investors or have the potential to do so with continued management changes or better economic conditions," he said.
